c.tagline: Sun-soaked university city near the Med, built around a grand medieval square.

taxi.fareNote: Official taxis are metered; fixed tariffs apply for airport runs.

emergency.note: 112 is the EU-wide emergency number; 15 reaches the SAMU ambulance service, 17 the police, and 18 the fire brigade.

avoid.reason: Pickpocketing in the centre and around the station

hood_desc: Montpellier's medieval historic core around the grand Place de la Comédie, a maze of pedestrian lanes lined with cafes, boutiques, and mansions; the best walkable base for first-timers.
Ricardo Bofill's monumental neoclassical quarter of wide boulevards and colonnades running from the old town to the Lez river; central, modern, and well served by tram.
An arty, leafy neighborhood just north of the center full of markets, independent cafes, and artists' studios; a relaxed, bohemian local feel.
A contemporary riverside district along the Lez with bold modern architecture and green spaces, popular with students and young families; lively bars and dining.
Calm residential streets below the Saint-Clément aqueduct and the Peyrou promenade, home to a beloved twice-weekly market; quiet and distinctly local.
lodging: Grand Hôtel du Midi Opéra Comédie

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink, as everywhere in France.

transit.hours: TaM trams run roughly 4:30am-1am (later on weekends), with buses on similar hours and a few night services; the four tram lines cover almost everything a visitor needs.
transit.note: TaM runs four colour-coded tram lines plus a dense bus network; the compact Écusson old town is largely pedestrian and best explored on foot.
transit.pay: Buy tickets from tram-stop machines or the TaM app and validate on boarding; a single ride is about €1.60 and a day pass about €4.20. Contactless bank-card tap-on is being rolled out.

bus: Montpellier Sabines coach station (Occitanie liO regional coaches)
FlixBus / BlaBlaCar Bus stops at Sabines
train: Gare Montpellier Sud de France (high-speed, southeast edge)

transit.m: Navette Aéroport shuttle (line 620) to Place de l'Europe, then tram to center (~30-40 min total)
Tram line 1 from Place de l'Europe to the city center (~15 min)

tip.r: Service is included by law (service compris); rounding up or leaving a euro or two for good service is appreciated but not expected.
